why: Only experiment that can un-provisional the causal sentence live on intellectualresistance.com. Literature (2506.09501, 2601.19934, 2604.22411) documents temp-0 across-run drift EXISTS but reports no magnitude for a fixed local model on a fixed bank — this run measures that magnitude in items. AMENDED 2026-07-28 after CS-003: fix batch size and seed and record both per run. That isolates the same residual arXiv:2601.19934 isolates (batch size 1, seeds fixed, still 0.093 unique-output fraction at temp 0), so our number sits beside a published one on the same mechanism. Zero extra cost — two settings, not more calls. Conditional on LM Studio exposing them; if not, record what they were. CONFIRMED (Hermes, 2026-07-28): executor already fixes eval_batch_size=4096, physical_batch_size=1024. Seed accepted by LM Studio at /api/v0/chat/completions but does NOT control kernel-level nondeterminism at temp 0 (residual is hardware FP ordering, not sampling). The comparison to published work is on batch-fixed terms; seed recorded per run for provenance but not expected to control the residual. COST CORRECTION 2026-07-28: this was carried as credits-gated. It is not — both runs used local LM Studio models, so there is no API bill; the only cost is machine time. BLOCKED ON CS-013 2026-07-28: fire after resume+load_epoch lands, so a mid-run crash costs one trial rather than 3.5h — and so a resumed run is detectable rather than silently mixing two model loads. PREDICTION WITHDRAWN 2026-07-29: I had recorded an expectation of ~0 changed items based on a 970-vs-974 comparison that is far likelier to be duplicate/shared-source rows (31 stochastic items matching exactly, joint p=3.4e-13 under independence). A pre-registration built on an artifact is worse than none — it launders the artifact into an expectation. THIS RUN FIRES WITH NO PRIOR. See inbox/claude-science/RETRACTION_zero_drift.md. REFRAMED 2026-07-29: with independence established and a rep-position effect ruled out, the surviving model is that reps are deterministic replays of accumulated state rather than independent draws. The replicate therefore tests REPLAY DETERMINISM. No prediction is registered — the replay model implies ~0 changed items, and registering that would launder a model into a confirmation. UNBLOCKED 2026-07-29 with a condition: resume shipped at 2c4ac652 but load_epoch did NOT (zero occurrences in mod.rs/main.rs/runs.rs, no migration). Firing anyway under a procedural guard stated in advance — completes-with-no-resume means clean data; any resume must be logged with run_id, resumed-from trial and wall-clock gap at the moment it happens; an unlogged resume makes the run unusable for the across-load question and it must be re-fired. Discipline-dependent rather than mechanical, which is strictly worse. Ruling: inbox/claude-science/RULING_fire_cs001.md IN FLIGHT 2026-07-29: Hermes reports run 985 executing, run 986 (CS-019 infra-guard test) queued behind it on the LM Studio serialization lock. title: Enforce migration 048's raw-id rule in CI so the fresh-seed check is a backstop, not the only defence
why: The bug the fresh-seed check catches has now happened TWICE. Migration 048 fixed the raw-id class and wrote the rule in its own header — never reference another row by raw id — and nothing enforced it, so 057 reintroduced it nine migrations later with WHERE id = 87, invisible to every local check because locally the row really was fixed. 060 repaired it by name. THE FRESH-SEED CHECK IS THE RIGHT BACKSTOP AND THE WRONG PRIMARY DEFENCE: it catches the consequence after the migration is written, at the cost of a full 58-migration replay, and only when someone remembers to run it. The rule itself is statically checkable — grep new migrations/*.sql for WHERE clauses matching id = <literal> against tests or any content table, and fail. That is a lint, it runs in milliseconds, it names the rule in its error message and it cannot be forgotten. A rule documented in a migration header is a comment; a rule in a linter is a rule — the same lesson as R7 in the board lint, which exists because a documented convention was breached three times. Pair it with the fresh-seed check rather than replacing it: the lint catches the known pattern, the fresh seed catches the unknown ones. DONE 2026-07-29 by claude-science rather than hermes: I asserted the rule was statically checkable, so the honest move was to build it rather than assign it. One design problem surfaced that the card did not anticipate — the lint correctly flags 057, which is APPLIED and cannot be edited, so a gate linting all migrations would fail forever on a defect already fixed, and a gate nobody can make green gets disabled. Solved with an explicit grandfather list rather than diff-only linting: diff detection silently stops checking anything if it breaks, and cannot run standalone, which this must while CI is down. The list is self-documenting — a future reader sees why 057 is exempt and that 060 fixed it. STILL NEEDS: wiring into ci.yml as a gate, which is hermes's lane and pointless until the billing lock clears.

Run against all 58 real migrations: exactly one hit — 057, the historical bug — now GRANDFATHERED by name with its reason and superseding fix (060) recorded in the code, because 057 is applied and immutable: editing it changes its checksum and breaks sqlx's _sqlx_migrations on every existing database.
